status_detail: Carbon County-provided release says one data-center proposal is currently being evaluated in Carbon County, located between Wellington and East Carbon, expected to use closed-loop cooling with less than 50 acre-feet/year water and self-generate electricity with natural gas. A Utah PMN-indexed Carbon County Planning Commission March 3, 2026 PDF also references a proposed data center and tax impacts, but the PDF text layer was not extractable.
notes: Developer not disclosed due to NDA language. Included under wide net because county-authored public release confirms an active proposal under evaluation.

notes: Checked county economic development pages and targeted searches for data center/server farm/planning references; current EDA projects list trails, CCC building, and other local projects, not data centers.

status_detail: Hill Air Force Base official article says DISA completed the Orion Cyber Operations Center-Hill, located on Hill Air Force Base in Davis County within the Ogden Data Center shared by DISA Hosting and Compute Center, DISA Global, and the DISA Global Service Desk.
notes: Also found a 2026 South Davis County data-center growth-potential PDF discussing feasible 10-120 MW edge/colocation/mid-scale facilities but no named South Davis project application.

project_name: Nine Mile / Uintah Basin Data Center
aliases: Wells Draw / South Myton Bench project
developer: Nine Mile Data LLC / Energence Utah LLC
status_detail: Public project information site and Basin Now report describe Nine Mile Data LLC's conditional-use permit request for a commercial data center in the South Myton Bench area; project information site says appeals were denied, while a Grand County staff inventory says conditional-use permit approval occurred in April 2026 and construction had not begun. Cleanview lists 400 MW on 475 acres, expected operational 2029.
notes: Capacity differs across public sources: Cleanview reports 400 MW; Grand County staff inventory reports 960+ acres rather than MW. County/project filings describe associated power, storage, solar, natural gas, and water/reuse infrastructure.

project_name: Unnamed Emery County data center prospect
aliases: Emery County potential data center development
status_detail: Emery County Planning Commission June 10, 2026 agenda and minutes discussed data center development; minutes state no formal application had been submitted but the county had received informal inquiries and could be a potential location because of land, energy infrastructure, and transmission. A Carbon County-provided July 2026 release also refers to a newer data center planned for Emery County designed to operate without water for cooling.
notes: No named applicant or parcel found. Included as early-stage/prospect under the brief's broad collection rule; mark low detail until a formal application appears.

status_detail: No data center project found in county planning/economic development pages or targeted web/news searches for Garfield County, Utah.
notes: County planning/economic-development page lists planning functions, plans, studies, business links, and staff contacts; searches for Garfield County Utah data center/server farm returned no local project evidence.

status_detail: Grand County Planning Commission May 26, 2026 staff report evaluated data-center policy and site feasibility, finding the county grid cannot support large-scale data centers and recommending code work before any application. The report states a future joint study session should occur before any formal application is received.
notes: Official/staff report discusses potential edge facilities and constraints, but no project application or named developer was found for Grand County.

status_detail: Iron County's data-center information page lists Antelope Data Center as a current application scheduled for June 4, 2026 Planning Commission review. Utah PMN agenda describes five approximately 1.35-million-square-foot buildings and an on-site data-center power plant scalable to 1.5 GW on about 640 acres along Antelope Springs Road; approved minutes show a motion to grant the CUP passed.
notes: County minutes describe phased buildout over approximately 8-10 years, about 250 acres developed within the 640-acre site, and one roughly 300 MW power-plant component per data-center building.

aliases: Red Butte Energy and Data Center Campus
Red Butte Data Center and Natural Gas Facilities Project
status_detail: Iron County official data-center information page says the Red Butte Data Center application was submitted May 4, 2026, deemed incomplete May 22, 2026, and is on hold under the county's 180-day moratorium adopted May 26, 2026. Secondary project writeups describe a 1.5 GW data center co-located with gas, battery, and solar resources.
notes: Official county page confirms application status but county-hosted document link is SharePoint-gated. Treat capacity/developer details as secondary-source until the county application package is directly accessible.

project_name: DCPC data center campus near Mona Reservoir
aliases: Data Center Power Company / DCPC Mona-area campus
status_detail: Juab County Planning Commission November 20, 2024 minutes approved a DCPC conditional-use permit for a data center north of Mona Reservoir on Boys Home Road, with conditions for road improvements, railroad crossing safety, water/wastewater state requirements, and code compliance. October 16, 2024 minutes describe 3-4 buildings of about 500,000 square feet each and on-site power generation.
notes: County records spell out DCPC as Data Center Power Collaboration. The county notice says the application was to construct and operate a data center campus with island power on listed parcels in Sections 5/6 T11S R1E and Sections 32/33 T10S R1E.

project_name: Summit Group Holdings / McWilliams-Sperry data center
status_detail: Juab County Planning Commission November 19, 2025 minutes state Ryan Matthews of Summit Group Holdings spoke for Jim McWilliams and Mike Sperry's zone change request, explaining the group had land under contract to develop a multi-billion-dollar data center; the Planning Commission recommended county commission approval of the zone change 3-2.
notes: Minutes describe proximity to power, transmission lines, gas, adjacent solar, closed-loop glycol cooling, possible trucked/tank water, 75-100 permanent jobs, and a 5-10+ year buildout. Later county approval was not confirmed in this pass.

project_name: Nebo North LLC data center campus
status_detail: Juab County public hearing notice for April 15, 2026 says Nebo North LLC applied for a conditional-use permit to construct and operate a data center campus on parcels XC00-2715-1, XC00-2710-, and XC00-2705 in Sections 13 and 14, Township 11 South, Range 1 West.
notes: Found public-hearing notice but did not confirm final action/approval in this pass.

project_name: BluSky AI Nephi modular AI infrastructure site
status_detail: Company announcement/search-indexed press says BluSky AI executed a non-binding LOI to lease about 16,000 square feet at 1358 N 200 W, Nephi, for modular AI infrastructure expansion; other company/newswire reporting says BluSky secured 9.3 MW of power and ground lease control for its first site. KUER reports Nephi adopted data-center zoning in late 2025 and multiple developers were interested near the Nephi airport.
notes: Capacity is reported as 9.3 MW power secured; datacentermap describes a 4 MW modular facility plus 9.3 MW solar/power access. Treat as announced/LOI until local permit or lease closing is verified.

status_detail: No Kane County data center project application found. Kane County Planning and Zoning February 11, 2026 agenda included a Wind/Solar/Data Center discussion, and minutes show public speakers requested safeguards against incompatible future uses such as a data center on a hotel/resort rezoning; applicants were willing to restrict uses via development agreement.
notes: County discussion indicates awareness/regulatory concern, not a named data-center project.
